the unit of analysis is defined as a player-referee dyad covering all encounters between them in the 2012-2013 season
the raw data contains 146,028 dyads
21,407 dyads (14.7%) were excluded for missing skin tone ratings (no profile photo)
this exclusion is characterized as a standard, data-quality-driven exclusion
the final analytic sample is N = 124,621 dyads
1,565 dyads (1.26%) had at least one red card
the outcome is defined as a binary indicator anyRedCard = 1 if redCards > 0, else 0
the primary exposure is defined as darkSkin = 1 if average skin tone ≥ 0.25, else 0
two independent raters coded each player's skin tone from photos on a 5-point scale
inter-rater reliability was excellent (Pearson r = 0.923)
skin tone was averaged across raters to create a continuous 0-1 scale
the specification search explored multiple cutoffs (0.125, 0.25, 0.375, 0.5, 0.625)
the 0.25 cutoff maximized the estimated effect size and minimized the p-value
0.25 was chosen as a conceptually defensible, substantive threshold
sensitivity analyses confirm robustness across cutoffs
the primary model was adjusted for a set of variables selected to control confounding and increase precision
games (count in dyad) was included as a covariate
games is treated as the primary measure of exposure (more games = more opportunity for red cards)
position category (5 levels, goalkeeper as reference) was included as a covariate
position is treated as a key confounder because defensive positions carry higher foul risk
missing position data (6.8%) was coded as an 'Unknown' category
age (continuous years, computed from birthday relative to July 1 2012) was included as a covariate
age is included because it may relate to aggression/disciplinary record
height (cm) was included as a covariate
height was median-imputed for 46 missing values (0.04%)
height is included because it may proxy for physicality
weight (kg) was included as a covariate
weight was median-imputed for 753 missing values (0.60%)
weight is included because it relates to physical play style
yellow cards (count in dyad) was included as a covariate for prior within-dyad disciplinary behavior
yellow cards is acknowledged as potentially also being a mediator rather than purely a confounder
including yellow cards is said to provide a conservative estimate of the effect
excluding yellow cards in a sensitivity analysis yields a similar effect
the covariates are described as standard controls for soccer disciplinary studies
median imputation for height/weight is described as standard and unlikely to bias results
logistic regression was used for the binary outcome
the model formula is anyRedCard ~ darkSkin + games + position_cat + age + height + weight + yellowCards
marginal standardization (g-computation) was used as the estimand method for the adjusted risk difference
the logistic model was fit to estimate the conditional odds of red cards
predicted probabilities of a red card were computed under two counterfactual scenarios
all players were set to dark skin (darkSkin = 1) in one counterfactual scenario
all players were set to light skin (darkSkin = 0) in the other counterfactual scenario
the risk difference was computed as the average difference in predicted probabilities between the two scenarios
the delta method via simulation was used for standard errors and confidence intervals
5,000 samples were drawn from the asymptotic normal distribution of the logistic regression coefficients using the estimated covariance matrix
the counterfactual risk difference was computed for each of the 5,000 draws
the 95% CI was defined as the 2.5th/97.5th percentiles of the 5,000 risk differences, and SE as their standard deviation
the two-sided p-value was computed as 2×(1 − Φ(|z|))
skin tone was transformed to a continuous 0-1 scale (average of rater1 and rater2), then dichotomized at 0.25
age was computed as a continuous variable from birthday
median imputation was used for missing height/weight, and an 'Unknown' category for missing position
no weighting was applied; each dyad was weighted equally
an alternative of weighting by number of games was considered but not used as the primary approach
sensitivity analyses show similar results with or without games weighting
no fixed effects were included in the primary specification

league fixed effects were deliberately excluded from the primary model because league is potentially a collider or mediator
